title: Flying Domestic in NZ with Kids — Air NZ Tips, Baggage, and Seat Selection
meta_desc: Flying domestic in NZ with kids? Get Air NZ tips, baggage info, and seat selection advice for a stress-free family trip
intro: As a parent, flying domestic in NZ with kids can be a daunting experience, especially when it comes to navigating Air NZ's baggage allowance and seat selection. With prices for a one-way Air NZ domestic ticket ranging from $50 to $200 NZD, it's essential to plan ahead to ensure a smooth and enjoyable trip for the whole family. In this article, we'll share our top tips for flying domestic in NZ with kids, including how to choose the best seats and make the most of your baggage allowance.

sections.heading: Air NZ Domestic Baggage Allowance
sections.body: Air NZ's domestic baggage allowance allows for one checked bag per person, with a maximum weight of 23kg. However, if you're travelling with kids, you may need to consider additional baggage for items like strollers, car seats, and port-a-cots. Air NZ allows these items to be checked for free, but it's essential to arrive early to ensure they are loaded onto the plane. The cost of checking an additional bag is $20-$30 NZD, depending on the route and time of booking.

sections.heading: Choosing the Best Seats for Your Family
list: Book seats together: Air NZ offers a range of seating options, including family-friendly seats with extra legroom.
Consider the exit row: If you're travelling with older kids, the exit row can provide more space and a more comfortable flying experience.
Avoid seats near the toilet: While it may seem convenient, seats near the toilet can be noisy and may have limited recline.

sections.heading: Tips for Flying with Infants
sections.body: If you're flying with an infant, it's essential to book a bassinet seat, which is available on most Air NZ domestic flights. These seats are designed for infants under 8 months and provide a safe and comfortable place for them to sleep. Additionally, Air NZ offers a range of infant-friendly amenities, including baby food and nappies.

sections.heading: Driving to the Airport: Time and Cost
sections.body: If you're driving to the airport, be sure to factor in traffic and parking costs. For example, driving from downtown Auckland to Auckland Airport can take around 30-40 minutes and cost $20-$30 NZD in parking fees. In contrast, driving from downtown Wellington to Wellington Airport takes around 15-20 minutes and costs $10-$20 NZD in parking fees.
